setlist.title: Untitled (I Might Compare) - this is a lyric from the Sweden era which JD dug up for that silent film score he did in 2010. other than that this is the only other recording of it I'm aware of. we still don't know its real title, if it had one
Birthday Song (This TIme Has Gone) - unreleased track played from the mid 90s to 2000ish mostly
My Favorite Things - probably the most well-known song on here, which is a wild thing to say. it's on a lot of bootlegs. I love John Coltrane!

Pure Change - that's what JD introduces it as but I always knew it as Pure Sun because of the one other recording. Song played once in like 1994 and then sometime last decade there was a show where he tried to remember it and only got through the first verse
Real Good Girlfriend - very cute song played once in Belgium about a month after this and then as far as I know never again. this recording is so amazing, gotta be my highlight
Are Friends Electric? (Gary Numan cover, two takes)

liner.body_md: This rare 1996 session captures the Mountain Goats performing for FSK Radio in Hamburg, Germany, during their tour with Cakekitchen [1]. The lineup features JD on guitar and vocals, Graeme Jefferies on piano, Markus Acher on percussion, and Peter Hughes on bass [1]. Taped by Gregor Kessler and transferred by notasfarwest, this twenty-four-minute recording is the only known archive of this specific performance [1]. It is the fifth show in the archive's collection for the band, following a concert in Bremen the previous day [2]. The setlist includes six tracks, all of which are firsts in the archive [1]. Highlights include a previously unknown song from the Sweden era, which JD later used for a 2010 silent film score [1]. The band also plays an unreleased track called Birthday Song, which they performed from the mid-90s until around 2000 [1]. My Favorite Things, a well-known bootleg track, is included alongside Pure Change, a song JD introduced by that name but which listeners often know as Pure Sun [1]. The performance of Real Good Girlfriend is particularly praised as a highlight, as the song was played only once elsewhere in Belgium [1]. The set concludes with two takes of a Gary Numan cover, Are Friends Electric? [1].
